entries.test: Documentation and demonstrations of major LLMs available on May 27, 2025 would establish whether nearly all supported both visual and audio inputs.
entries.note: The test must preserve 'basically every,' rather than require every model without exception.

entries.test: Consumer AI hardware sales and usage through publication, together with OpenAI's contemporaneous valuation and the proposed $1 trillion addition, would test both assertions.
entries.note: Zitron endorses the adoption claim and valuation comparison, while mocking Altman's suggested value gain.
The proposition evaluates the expectation as 'insane'; its central commitment is a judgment of plausibility.
The launch condition is preserved, but 'really good' supplies no agreed standard of quality.
The overall proposition is an evaluative characterization of the deal. It also attributes private feelings to investors.

entries.test: Public releases, functionality, and consumer adoption of LLM-based products by May 27, 2025 would establish whether any substantive consumer product besides ChatGPT existed.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph explicitly supplies the ChatGPT exception. The plain reading concerns actual consumer offerings.

entries.test: Stargate financing agreements and contemporaneous reporting on SoftBank's fundraising would establish its financial responsibility and whether raising the initial $100 billion was encountering difficulties.
entries.note: This describes the financing arrangement and fundraising status at publication.
Both assertions are explicitly framed as appearances through 'seem,' rather than firm claims about access or construction.

entries.test: Oracle's and Crusoe's prior data-center project records, alongside public accounts of repeated OpenAI demand forecasts and resulting server-capacity shortfalls, would test the three assertions.
entries.note: Context identifies 'never done this' as Crusoe's lack of previous AI data-center construction experience. Outages alone would not establish underestimation.
The combined statement is an insult and sweeping exaggeration. Specific product-release or commoditization assertions would need separate records.
